reasoning: Both sets cover all three stages on one shared rllab package, with code-shaped contracts, a Phase 0 interface task, spine, wiring and system phases, and valid dependency graphs. B is the stronger RL design. It follows the brief closely: a circular tank, survival as the fish score, and a self-play opponent pool with cross-play. Its learning ladders (tabular to DQN to CNN with ablations; REINFORCE to PPO; fixed opponents to naive co-learning to a pool) are sound, it keeps truncation separate from termination, and its golden cases give exact board coordinates and closed-form GAE and clipped-objective answers. Its planning structure is weaker. There is one huge milestone per stage, with no walking skeleton: M1 bundles tabular, DQN, CNN, ablations, the SB3 reference, the corridor, replay and reporting. B's M1 interface freezes fish, predator-prey and self-play types that no M1 task uses. The system task is sized S but covers every real 5-seed ladder and reference run. The brief is stale: it still says it is "Not doing: Designing future environments now" and gives success only for Snake. A is better as a build plan. M1 is a true walking skeleton: a minimal online Q-learning spine runs through a check-world gate, batch training, live progress, charts and a rigorous paired-permutation final evaluation. A freezes only M1 boundaries and explicitly lists the boundaries it leaves unfrozen. Its spec is more precise on statistics. A has real faults. It turns the circular tank into a square one and makes the fish score hits with respawn instead of survival time. Predator-prey has no opponent pool, so self-play is weaker. Milestones are numbered out of build order (M5 and M6 come before M4), M2 is a grab-bag of leftovers, and some packets leave out needed types. On balance, A's cleaner milestone slicing, interface discipline and consistency edge out B's richer but heavier plan.

strengths: M1 is a real walking skeleton: online Q-learning and REINFORCE spines are true minimal baselines, not mocks
Method check worlds (two-exit corridor, 1-D target) gate every batch with hand-derived answers
EVAL-04 fully specifies a paired permutation test with Holm correction; TC-19 checks Holm by closed form
The interface task freezes only M1 boundaries; unfrozen symbols are listed explicitly for later milestones
Clear separation of entries (AD-10), with cli owning no pipeline step
weaknesses: Fish tank is a square with respawn-on-hit scoring, not the brief's circular tank where fish survive as long as possible
Predator-prey has no opponent pool or self-play mechanism, only simultaneous co-training plus a pairing grid
Milestone IDs run out of build order (M1, M2, M3, M5, M6, M4); M2 bundles DQN thickening, replay, video, refcheck and notes
M1 doesn't let the user watch a replay or see the snake beat the baselines; both are deferred to M2
Some golden cases are property checks over generated rollouts instead of concrete expected states (TC-06, TC-12)

strengths: Faithful to the brief: circular tank, survival time as the score, limited vision, self-play with an opponent pool and cross-play generations
Rich, sound RL ladders (tabular/DQN/CNN plus ablations; REINFORCE vs PPO; three self-play rungs) that each teach one concept
Very concrete golden cases with exact boards, positions and closed-form GAE and clipped-objective values
Careful truncation vs termination handling and a one-to-one SB3 settings mapping, so a reference gap points at the learner's code
Split packets such as M1-T13 are fully self-sufficient
weaknesses: One giant milestone per stage, with no walking skeleton; M1 alone covers the corridor, tabular, DQN, CNN, ablations, SB3 reference, report and replay
The M1 interface freezes S2/S3 types (FishTank, PPOAgent, OpponentPool, PredatorPrey) that no M1 task needs
M1-T31 is sized S but runs every real 5-seed ladder, ablation and reference job plus all QRs
Stale brief: says it is not designing future environments, and success criteria cover Snake only
Statistical claims pool games across seeds and leave the test choice to the skill, which is less rigorous than a fixed paired design
